response_text:
## California Security Deposit After Move-Out

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

In California, a landlord generally must return the security deposit or provide an itemized statement of deductions within **21 days** after the tenant moves out. If it has been **30 days** since the **2026-02-28** move-out date and nothing has been returned, the tenant should move quickly, preserve evidence, and send a written demand.

## Practical Tenant Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check2-square.svg

- Confirm the move-out date and calculate the deadline: **2026-03-21** was the 21-day deadline.
- Gather proof that the unit was left clean and undamaged.
- Send a written demand for the full deposit and an itemized explanation of any claimed deductions.
- Use a traceable delivery method and keep proof of sending.
- If the landlord still does not respond, consider small claims court or local tenant legal aid.

## What to Gather Before Sending the Demand

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/folder2-open.svg

- Lease or rental agreement
- Move-in and move-out inspection reports, if any
- Photos and videos showing the apartment was clean and left in good condition
- Dated photos if available, plus original files/metadata
- Move-out notice or email confirming surrender of possession
- Proof of deposit payment, such as a canceled check, bank record, or receipt
- Any texts or emails with the landlord about the deposit
- Forwarding address you gave the landlord
- Mail receipt or tracking proof for the demand letter
- Receipts for any cleaning or repair work you paid for

## Sample Written Demand Letter Outline

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/envelope-paper.svg

- **Your name and forwarding address**
- **Landlord’s name and mailing address**
- **Date**
- **Property address**
- **Subject:** Demand for Return of Security Deposit
- **Short facts:** you moved out on **2026-02-28**, left the unit clean, and have photos
- **Legal point:** the 21-day deadline has passed and no deposit or itemized statement was received
- **Demand:** return the full deposit immediately, or send a lawful itemized statement and any remaining balance
- **Deadline to comply:** give a short deadline, such as 7 to 10 days from receipt
- **Delivery method:** state that you are sending the letter by certified mail or another trackable method
- **Closing:** request written response and include your signature

### Simple Demand Wording
- “I moved out of the property on 2026-02-28 and left the unit clean and in good condition, as shown by the attached photos.”
- “California law generally requires return of the security deposit or an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out.”
- “Because I have not received either, I demand immediate return of my security deposit in full, or a proper itemized statement with supporting deductions.”
- “Please respond within 10 days of receipt of this letter.”

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg

- Waiting too long to act after the 21-day deadline passes
- Sending only a text message instead of a formal written demand
- Not keeping copies of photos, letters, and mailing receipts
- Forgetting to include a forwarding address
- Arguing only verbally without a paper trail
- Assuming the landlord can keep the deposit without giving any explanation
- Claiming “clean” without preserving dated photos or other proof
- Ignoring possible deductions for unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear, or cleaning needed to restore the unit to the same level of cleanliness as at move-in

## Next Best Steps

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/arrow-right-circle.svg

- Send the demand letter now by certified mail with return receipt, if possible.
- Keep a complete copy of everything you send.
- If the landlord does not pay, file in small claims court and bring your photos, lease, deposit proof, and mailing receipts.

## Sources

- California Civil Code, security deposit rules: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1950.5&lawCode=CIV
- California Courts self-help: https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/
- California Department of Consumer Affairs, landlord-tenant guidance: https://www.dca.ca.gov/publications/landlordbook/tenant-deposit.shtml

response_text:
## College Laptop Fit Snapshot
A strong student laptop here should prioritize **16 GB RAM**, **sub-1.5 kg weight**, and enough storage for coding projects and creative files. Given the $1,100 cap, the best balance is the one that stays within budget without giving up too much on performance or portability.

## Laptop Comparison and Best Pick
| Option | Screen | RAM | Storage | Weight | Price | Fit for your use |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Option A | 14-inch | 16 GB | 512 GB SSD | 1.3 kg | $999 | Best overall balance |
| Option B | 15-inch | 8 GB | 512 GB SSD | 1.4 kg | $849 | Cheaper, but weaker for coding and editing |
| Option C | 13-inch | 16 GB | 1 TB SSD | 1.2 kg | $1,149 | Best specs, but over budget |

**Recommendation: Option A**

Why it wins:
- **16 GB RAM** is the biggest practical advantage for coding, multitasking, and light photo editing.
- **1.3 kg** fits your portability preference comfortably.
- **$999** stays inside budget, leaving room for accessories or software.
- **14-inch** is a good middle ground for note-taking and editing without feeling cramped.

Trade-offs:
- **512 GB SSD** is fine for college use, but less generous than Option C’s 1 TB.
- It is not the lightest option, but the difference vs. Option C is small enough that the budget savings matter more.
- If you store lots of raw photos or large projects locally, you may eventually want external storage or cloud backup.

## Best Choice at a Glance
- **Pick Option A** if you want the best all-around laptop for school, coding, and light creative work.
- **Pick Option C** only if you can stretch the budget by $49 and value extra storage more than staying under budget.
- **Skip Option B** unless price is your top priority, because **8 GB RAM** is the main bottleneck for your workload.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: See student laptop tips] https://www.example.com

- General laptop buying guidance: https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-laptops
- Student laptop considerations: https://www.pcworld.com/article/394449/best-laptops-for-college-students.html

response_text:
## Kyoto 2-Day Sightseeing Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

A balanced spring plan for **2 adults** with a **¥18,000 per person activity budget** and **under 12,000 steps/day**. It prioritizes temples, one scenic neighborhood walk, and a rain-friendly indoor backup while keeping coffee and dinner built in each day.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Route
| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | Est. per person |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apr 10 | **Kiyomizu-dera** early visit; start before crowds | **Sannenzaka / Ninenzaka** scenic walk, then **Yasaka Shrine** area | Coffee break near Gion, then **Pontocho / Kamo River** dinner stroll | **¥6,000–¥8,000** |
| Apr 11 | **Fushimi Inari Taisha** short loop to the first scenic viewpoints | **Nishiki Market** lunch + **Kyoto International Manga Museum** or **Kyoto Railway Museum** if it rains | Coffee break, then **To-ji** or **Gion evening walk** and sit-down dinner | **¥6,500–¥9,000** |

## Kyoto Sightseeing Blocks
### Day 1: Higashiyama Temples and Old Streets
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Kiyomizu-dera, then a short temple-to-street descent through the preserved lanes.
- **Afternoon:** Walk Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka at an easy pace; continue to Yasaka Shrine and the edge of Gion.
- **Coffee break:** Stop in Gion or Higashiyama for matcha latte / drip coffee.
- **Evening:** Sit-down dinner near Pontocho or along the Kamo River.
- **Step target:** about **8,000–10,500** depending on pace and photo stops.
- **Rain backup:** Kyoto National Museum area or a covered café-and-gallery stop in central Kyoto.

### Day 2: Fushimi Inari + Central Kyoto Indoor Backup
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Fushimi Inari Taisha; keep it to the lower trails and viewpoint loop to stay within your step limit.
- **Afternoon:** Nishiki Market for lunch, then choose an indoor option if the weather turns wet.
- **Coffee break:** Central Kyoto café stop after the market.
- **Evening:** To-ji for a calm temple finish, or a light Gion walk if you want a second scenic neighborhood.
- **Step target:** about **9,000–11,500** with a shortened shrine route.
- **Rain backup:** Kyoto International Manga Museum for a low-cost indoor activity.

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-yen.svg
- **Temple admissions:** mostly low-cost; plan around **¥1,000–¥2,500/day per person**.
- **Coffee:** budget **¥600–¥1,200/day per person**.
- **Dinner:** budget **¥2,000–¥4,000/day per person** for a comfortable sit-down meal.
- **Indoor backup:** keep **¥500–¥1,500** per person reserved for museum entry if needed.
- **Total target:** comfortably fits inside **¥18,000 per person** for the trip’s activity and meal mix.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Rain Backup Ideas] https://www.kyototourism.org/en/
Action: [Button: Temple Hours] https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2158.html

- Kyoto travel guide: https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2158.html
- Kyoto weather context: https://www.timeanddate.com/weather/japan/kyoto

| 2 | 2017 Honda Civic | $15,200 | 74,000 | **Very good** | **Very high** | **Low** | Great car, but higher miles and more wear than the Corolla |
| 3 | 2019 Mazda3 | $16,400 | 58,000 | **Good** | **High** | **Low to moderate** | Nicer drive and newer, but over budget and typically pricier to insure/repair |

## What Each One Means for You

### 1) 2018 Toyota Corolla
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/car-front.svg
- **Best overall fit** for a first-time buyer who wants predictable ownership.
- Toyota parts, service, and repairs are usually straightforward and affordable.
- At **62k miles**, it is still in a comfortable range if maintenance history is clean.
- Trade-off: it is the least exciting to drive and may feel basic inside.

### 2) 2017 Honda Civic
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/car-front.svg
- Very close second; also a strong reliability choice.
- The big downside is **74k miles**, which is noticeably more wear than the Corolla and Mazda3.
- If it has better service records, new tires, or recent maintenance, it could move ahead in real-world value.
- Trade-off: slightly more risk from age/miles, even though the model is excellent overall.

### 3) 2019 Mazda3
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/car-front.svg
- Best driving feel and newest model year here.
- But it is **over your budget by $400**, which matters because you should keep a repair cushion.
- Mazda3 ownership can still be reliable, but parts, tires, and some repairs can cost a bit more than a Corolla.
- Trade-off: nicer car, but not the best match for a strict low-cost ownership goal.

## Plain-English Recommendation

**Buy the Corolla if your priority is low stress and low total cost.**
It gives you the best balance of price, mileage, and long-term reliability for a first-time buyer.

**Choose the Civic only if its maintenance history is clearly better** than the Corolla’s.
If it has documented service, a clean inspection, and recent wear items replaced, it can be nearly as strong a buy.

**Skip the Mazda3 unless the seller drops the price below $16,000** and the car has exceptional records.
It is the nicest of the three, but it is not the strongest value for your budget and ownership goals.

## Berlin 12-Month Lease Pre-Sign Checklist
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

A practical sign-before-you-pay checklist for a **1-bedroom, 42 m²** apartment starting **2026-08-01** at **€1,250 warm**. Use it to confirm total costs, deposit handling, and who fixes what before you commit.

## Questions to Ask Before You Sign
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check2-square.svg

- **Total monthly payment**
  - What exactly is included in the **€1,250 warm rent**?
  - Is heating, hot water, building cleaning, garbage, and internet included or excluded?
  - Are there any separate monthly charges for electricity, gas, TV/radio fee, or parking?

- **Deposit terms**
  - How much is the **Kaution** in euros, and is it capped at the usual legal maximum?
  - Can the deposit be paid in **3 installments**?
  - Where will the deposit be held, and will I get written confirmation?
  - What deductions are allowed at move-out, and what proof is required?

- **Repair responsibility**
  - Which repairs are the landlord’s responsibility versus mine?
  - Who handles **heating, boiler, plumbing leaks, windows, appliances, and electrical faults**?
  - Is there a list of small repairs I must pay for, and what is the maximum amount per repair?
  - How should I report urgent repairs, and what response time is expected?

- **Move-in condition**
  - Will we do a **signed handover protocol** with photos and meter readings?
  - What existing damage will be documented before move-in?
  - Are all keys, fobs, cellar access, and mailbox keys included?

- **Lease costs and surprises**
  - Are there any **broker fees, admin fees, cleaning fees, or move-in charges**?
  - Will the rent increase during the 12-month term, and under what condition?
  - Are utility advances estimated realistically for a 42 m² apartment?

- **House rules and use**
  - Are subletting, pets, smoking, or renovations allowed?
  - Are there quiet hours, bike storage rules, or shared laundry rules?
  - Is the apartment furnished, and if so, what inventory is included?

## Signing-Ready Checklist
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/list-check.svg

- Ask for the **full rental breakdown in writing** before signing.
- Confirm the **deposit amount, payment schedule, and return conditions**.
- Get the **repair responsibilities** written into the lease or annex.
- Inspect the apartment and document **all defects, meter readings, and key counts**.
- Verify the **lease end date, renewal terms, and notice period**.
- Keep copies of the **contract, handover protocol, and any email promises**.

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Lease Review] https://www.berlin.de/sen/wohnen/
Action: [Button: Tenant Help] https://www.mieterbund.de/

## Sources
- Berlin Senate housing information: https://www.berlin.de/sen/wohnen/
- German Tenants’ Association: https://www.mieterbund.de/
- German Civil Code overview: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/

# Junior Data Analyst Application for Toronto

## Tailored Resume Summary
**Junior Data Analyst** with 1 year of internship experience supporting reporting, dashboarding, and data quality tasks. Skilled in **Excel, SQL, and basic Tableau**, with a strong focus on turning messy data into clear insights for stakeholders. Comfortable working in **hybrid environments** and contributing to recurring reporting, dashboard maintenance, and cross-functional communication.

## Resume Bullets for Dashboarding, Reporting, and Stakeholder Communication
- Built and maintained **Tableau dashboards** to track key performance metrics, helping teams monitor trends and identify issues faster.
- Used **SQL** to extract, clean, and validate data for recurring reports, improving accuracy and reducing manual effort.
- Created **Excel-based reports and templates** for weekly and monthly updates, streamlining reporting workflows for internal stakeholders.
- Partnered with team members to gather reporting requirements, clarify metric definitions, and deliver outputs aligned with business needs.
- Communicated findings in concise, stakeholder-friendly summaries, translating data into actionable recommendations for non-technical audiences.

## Cover Letter Outline
### Opening Paragraph
- State interest in the Junior Data Analyst role in Toronto.
- Mention 1 year of internship experience and hands-on work with Excel, SQL, and Tableau.
- Note enthusiasm for dashboarding, reporting, and stakeholder-facing work in a **hybrid** setting.

### Middle Paragraph 1: Relevant Experience
- Describe internship experience supporting reporting cycles, dashboard updates, or data validation.
- Highlight examples of building reports, cleaning datasets, or improving data accuracy.
- Emphasize ability to work with multiple stakeholders and respond to changing priorities.

### Middle Paragraph 2: Role Fit
- Connect your skills to the job requirements: dashboarding, recurring reporting, and communication.
- Mention comfort with turning data into clear insights for business users.
- Briefly note that your salary target is **CAD 62,000–70,000**, aligned with the role and market.

### Closing Paragraph
- Reaffirm interest in contributing to the team.
- Mention openness to **hybrid work only**.
- End with a confident, professional close and invitation to discuss fit.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Cover letter tips] https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/findajob/resources/cover-letter

- Government of Canada Job Bank: https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/home
- Government of Canada job search resources: https://www.canada.ca/en/services/jobs.html

response_text:
## Barcelona Family Trip at a Relaxed Pace

A low-stress 5-day plan for 2 adults + 1 child age 7, built around **one museum day, one beach day, one food-focused evening, and one flexible rest half-day**. It keeps the pace to **no more than 2 major activities per day** and stays within the **€1,600 total budget excluding flights**.

## Day-by-Day Barcelona Itinerary

### Day 1 — Tue, 2026-07-14: Easy Arrival + Old Town Stroll
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, unpack, and keep the first few hours open for a slow start.
- **Afternoon:** Gentle walk through the Gothic Quarter and a short stop near the cathedral area.
- **Dinner:** Simple tapas dinner near your hotel so everyone can reset early.
- **Budget target:** **€180–€240**

### Day 2 — Wed, 2026-07-15: Museum Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **CosmoCaixa** for an easy, child-friendly museum experience.
- **Afternoon:** Light lunch nearby, then return to the hotel for downtime or a pool break.
- **Dinner:** Casual neighborhood meal with kid-friendly options.
- **Budget target:** **€200–€280**

### Day 3 — Thu, 2026-07-16: Beach Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Morning:** Head to **Barceloneta Beach** early before the strongest heat.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/92/194_White-nosed_coati_at_the_beach_in_Yucat%C3%A1n_Photo_by_Giles_Laurent.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original Alt=Morning:** Head to **Barceloneta Beach** early before the strongest heat, Rest
- **Afternoon:** Keep it simple: sand time, snacks, and a shaded break; no extra sightseeing.
- **Dinner:** Easy seafood or rice dishes near the waterfront, or back near your hotel if the child is tired.
- **Budget target:** **€220–€300**

### Day 4 — Fri, 2026-07-17: Flexible Half-Day + Food-Focused Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Morning:** Flexible rest half-day: sleep in, laundry, pool time, or a quiet park visit.
- **Afternoon:** Very light activity only if everyone feels up to it, such as a short café stop.
- **Evening:** Make this the big food night: early dinner, shared plates, dessert stop, and a relaxed walk afterward.
- **Budget target:** **€260–€360**

### Day 5 — Sat, 2026-07-18: Gentle Departure Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg
- **Morning:** Pack, check out, and keep the schedule open.
- **Afternoon:** If timing allows, one final low-key lunch or souvenir stop.
- **Dinner:** Departure meal as needed depending on flight time.
- **Budget target:** **€120–€180**

## Budget Plan for the Full Trip

- **Accommodation:** €700–€900
- **Food and drinks:** €420–€520
- **Local transport:** €70–€120
- **Museum and beach extras:** €60–€120
- **Flex buffer:** €150–€200

**Estimated total:** **€1,400–€1,600**

## Best Low-Stress Choices by Day

- **Museum day:** CosmoCaixa is the strongest fit for a 7-year-old and keeps the day engaging without feeling intense.
- **Beach day:** Barceloneta works best for convenience, with easy access and simple logistics.
- **Food evening:** Choose a place with an early reservation and a menu that includes tapas, grilled items, and dessert.
- **Rest half-day:** Keep it truly open; this is the best way to protect energy and avoid overload.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Museum Pick] https://www.cosmocaixa.es/en
Action: [Button: Beach Info] https://www.barcelona.cat/en/what-to-do-in-bcn/beaches/barceloneta-beach
Action: [Button: Family Transit] https://www.tmb.cat/en/home

## Sources

- CosmoCaixa Barcelona: https://www.cosmocaixa.es/en
- Barcelona beaches overview: https://www.barcelona.cat/en/what-to-do-in-bcn/beaches/barceloneta-beach
- Barcelona public transport: https://www.tmb.cat/en/home

## Sales Dashboard Snapshot for Q1 2026
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/graph-up.svg

Your dataset is small but strong enough for a clear executive dashboard: it shows monthly performance for **North** and **South** across **units sold** and **revenue**. The best presentation will emphasize trend, region comparison, and the relationship between volume and revenue.

## Recommended Charts and Key Insights
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/bar-chart.svg

### Best chart types
- **Line chart** for monthly trend
  - Use 2 lines for revenue by region, or 2 lines for units sold by region.
  - Best for showing the rise from January to March and the February peak in North.
- **Clustered column chart** for region comparison by month
  - Show North vs South side by side for each month.
  - Best for quick stakeholder comparison.
- **Combo chart** for units and revenue together
  - Columns for units sold, line for revenue.
  - Best for showing whether revenue is tracking with volume.
- **KPI cards** for top-line metrics
  - Total revenue, total units sold, best month, best region.
- **Scatter or bubble chart** if you want a “sales efficiency” view
  - X-axis: units sold, Y-axis: revenue, one point per region-month.
  - Best for spotting whether higher unit volume always means higher revenue.

### Key insights to highlight
- **North leads overall** in both units and revenue across all three months.
- **March is the strongest month for South** on revenue and units, narrowing the gap with North.
- **North peaks in February** with the highest revenue in the dataset at **52,000**.
- **Revenue and units move together** fairly closely, suggesting consistent pricing or product mix.
- **Total Q1 performance**
  - Units sold: **712**
  - Revenue: **274,100**
- **Regional totals**
  - North: **383 units**, **146,800 revenue**
  - South: **329 units**, **127,300 revenue**

### Compact data view
Month | North Units | North Revenue | South Units | South Revenue
2026-01 | 120 | 45,000 | 98 | 38,500
2026-02 | 135 | 52,000 | 110 | 41,200
2026-03 | 128 | 49,800 | 121 | 47,600

## Simple Dashboard Layout for a Business Presentation
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/layout-text-window-reverse.svg

### Top row: executive KPIs
- **Total Revenue**
- **Total Units Sold**
- **Best Performing Month**
- **Top Region**

### Middle row: trend and comparison
- **Left panel:** Revenue trend line chart by month and region
- **Right panel:** Clustered bar chart for units sold by month and region

### Bottom row: performance context
- **Left panel:** Combo chart showing units and revenue together
- **Right panel:** Insight box with 3 bullets:
  - North is consistently ahead
  - South is improving fastest by March
  - February is the strongest month overall for revenue

### Optional presentation-friendly structure
- **Slide 1:** KPI overview
- **Slide 2:** Monthly trend chart
- **Slide 3:** Regional comparison chart
- **Slide 4:** Insights and action recommendations

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Create presentation] https://www.canva.com/

## Manchester Bathroom Leak: Homeowner Repair Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

A leak that shows up after heavy showers is usually a **water-management problem** rather than a full structural failure. With an **18-year-old** house and a **£900 cap**, the best approach is to check the simplest shower-side causes first, then move to ceiling/plumbing repairs only if the source is confirmed.

## Step-by-Step Troubleshooting and Repair Order
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clipboard-check.svg

| Priority | Check / Repair | What to Look For | Typical Cost Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Shower screen/curtain sealing | Water escaping at the edge during long showers | £0–£80 |
| 2 | Grout and silicone | Cracked, missing, or mouldy sealant around shower, tray, bath, or tiles | £50–£180 |
| 3 | Shower tray or bath edge | Water pooling or running under the tray/along the bath lip | £80–£250 |
| 4 | Waste/drain connection | Drips only when shower is running; damp patch near pipe route | £120–£300 |
| 5 | Ceiling access check | Staining, soft plaster, or active dripping below bathroom | £100–£350 |
| 6 | Localized ceiling repair | Patch, dry out, stain block, repaint after the source is fixed | £150–£450 |

### Practical Troubleshooting Checklist
- Run one **short shower**, then one **long shower**, and watch exactly when the leak starts.
- Check whether water appears only when the shower is aimed at one side of the enclosure.
- Look closely at the **sealant line** around the shower tray, bath, screen, and tile edges.
- Press gently on the bathroom ceiling below the leak for any **soft or swollen areas**.
- Check for water tracking near the **waste pipe** or around the shower tray base.
- If safe, inspect the loft or space above the ceiling for **damp timber, water marks, or dripping**.
- Dry the area fully, then repeat the shower test to confirm whether the issue is still active.
- Take photos before and after each test so you can compare the leak pattern.

## Likely Causes in Order of Probability
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg

1. **Failed silicone seal around the shower or bath**
   - Most common if the leak appears only after heavy showers.
   - Water slips behind the enclosure and travels to the ceiling below.

2. **Cracked grout or tile edge gaps**
   - Common in older bathrooms where movement has opened small gaps.
   - Usually worse when water hits one wall repeatedly.

3. **Shower screen or tray edge not sealing properly**
   - Water can escape at the door edge or tray joint and work downward.

4. **Loose waste or pipe joint**
   - More likely if the leak happens even with careful shower use.
   - Often leaves a persistent damp patch rather than a random one.

5. **Damaged ceiling plaster from repeated moisture**
   - The ceiling may be showing the symptom, not the source.
   - Needs drying and repair only after the leak source is fixed.

## Repair Priority Within a £900 Cap
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-pound.svg

- **First spend:** sealant, grout touch-ups, and any obvious enclosure gaps.
- **Second spend:** plumbing inspection of the shower waste and nearby joints if the leak continues.
- **Third spend:** ceiling patching and repainting only after the source is stopped.
- **Hold back budget:** keep at least **£200–£300** for a plumber or follow-up repair if the first fix does not solve it.

### Sensible Budget Split
- Sealant/grout materials and basic tools: **£20–£60**
- Handyperson or bathroom seal repair: **£80–£200**
- Plumber call-out and minor repair: **£120–£300**
- Ceiling patch and repaint: **£150–£350**
- Contingency for a second visit or extra materials: **£150–£250**

## Quick Actions
- Action: [Button: Check seals] https://www.wickes.co.uk/ideas-advice/repair-and-maintenance
- Action: [Button: Find a plumber] https://www.checkatrade.com/blog/trade/plumbers/
- Action: [Button: Ceiling repair guide] https://www.diy.com/help-advice

## Friday Night Movie Night Picks
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/play-circle.svg

A good fit for your group means: suspenseful but not intense, clean enough for a teen, and short enough to keep the night moving. I mixed older and newer titles, with a lean toward fun tension over gore.

## 6 Light-Suspense Movies Under 120 Minutes
| Title | Year | Runtime | Why it fits |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Rear Window | 1954 | 112 min | Classic suspense with playful tension, no gore, and a great “everyone can guess along” mystery vibe. |
| Charade | 1963 | 113 min | A stylish, witty thriller-romance with light danger, fast pacing, and very Friday-night friendly energy. |
| Clue | 1985 | 94 min | Comedy-mystery with suspenseful twists, zero gore, and lots of group-friendly laughs. |
| The Game | 1997 | 129 min | Strong suspense and a fun twist-heavy setup, but it slightly misses your runtime limit; best as a backup only. |
| See How They Run | 2022 | 98 min | Modern whodunit with light suspense, English dialogue, and a playful tone that stays accessible for a teen. |
| A Haunting in Venice | 2023 | 103 min | Moody mystery with restrained scares rather than gore, making it a good “just spooky enough” option. |

## Best Fit for Your Group
- **Top pick: Clue** — shortest, funniest, and easiest to enjoy as a mixed-age group without stress or gore.
- **Best classic: Rear Window** — more suspenseful and elegant, but still clean and under 120 minutes.
- **Best newer option: See How They Run** — modern pacing, light suspense, and a comfortable Friday-night watch.
- **Best if you want slightly spookier: A Haunting in Venice** — atmospheric and tense, but not graphic.

## Quick Actions

- Action: [Button: Check streaming availability] https://www.justwatch.com/

- Streaming availability lookup: https://www.justwatch.com/

## Monthly Budget Snapshot

Your monthly take-home pay is **$4,800** and your planned spending plus savings comes to **$4,035**, leaving **$765** unassigned. That gives you room to strengthen savings or build a buffer.

## Category-by-Category Allocation

| Category | Amount | Share of Income |
|---|---:|---:|
| Rent | $1,650 | 34.4% |
| Utilities | $220 | 4.6% |
| Groceries | $450 | 9.4% |
| Transit | $130 | 2.7% |
| Subscriptions | $45 | 0.9% |
| Student loan | $310 | 6.5% |
| Savings goal | $700 | 14.6% |
| Dining out | $250 | 5.2% |
| Phone | $80 | 1.7% |
| Miscellaneous | $200 | 4.2% |
| Unassigned buffer | $765 | 15.9% |

### Budget Readout
- **Fixed essentials:** Rent, utilities, transit, phone, and student loan total **$2,390**.
- **Flexible spending:** Groceries, dining out, subscriptions, and miscellaneous total **$945**.
- **Savings:** Your current savings target is **$700**, which is healthy at **14.6%** of income.
- **Leftover room:** The **$765 buffer** is the main opportunity to improve savings or prepare for irregular costs.

## Overspending Risk Check

- **Rent risk:** At **34.4%** of income, rent is high but still manageable.
- **Dining out risk:** **$250** is the most likely category to creep upward if you eat out more often.
- **Miscellaneous risk:** **$200** can easily absorb small extras and become a leak.
- **Subscriptions risk:** Small individually, but worth reviewing if any are unused.
- **Groceries risk:** Reasonable now, but inflation could push this category above plan.

## Two Ways to Increase Savings

- **Move the full buffer to savings:** Redirect the **$765 unassigned amount** into savings, raising monthly savings from **$700 to $1,465** without changing rent or transit.
- **Trim flexible spending and redirect it:** Cut **dining out by $100** and **miscellaneous by $100** and add that **$200** to savings, bringing total savings to **$1,665** if you also use the buffer.

## Practical Next Move

- Keep your current savings goal as the minimum.
- Treat the **$765 buffer** as “extra savings unless needed.”
- If you want a tighter plan, start by capping **dining out** and **miscellaneous** first.

## Sources

- Budgeting guidance: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/budgeting/
- 50/30/20 framework overview: https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/spending-saving-budgeting/budgeting

response_text:
## QR Scanner Retail Flow

A simple, fast in-store flow works best for retail staff: scan, confirm product details, add to cart, and recover cleanly from invalid codes. The design below keeps each state lightweight and optimized for one-handed use.

## Screen Flow and State Layout

### 1) Scan Screen
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg
- Full-screen camera preview with a centered scan frame.
- Top bar: store name, flashlight toggle, and history shortcut.
- Bottom sheet: scan tips and recent scan status.
- Primary action: auto-detect QR and open product details instantly.

### 2) Product Detail Card
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/bag-check.svg
- Show **Product Name** in large type.
- Show **Price** directly below the name.
- Show **Stock Status** as a clear badge:
  - In stock
  - Low stock
  - Out of stock
- Include a prominent **Add to Cart** button.
- Secondary actions: rescan, open history, view cart.

### 3) Invalid Code State
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg
- Message: “This QR code is not recognized.”
- Short helper text: “Try scanning again or enter the product manually.”
- Primary action: **Rescan**
- Secondary action: **Manual Entry**
- Keep the camera visible in the background so the user can recover quickly.

### 4) Recent Scans Screen
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock-history.svg
- Show the last **5 scans** in a compact list.
- Each row includes:
  - Product name
  - Price
  - Stock badge
  - Timestamp
- Tapping a row reopens the product detail card.
- Add a “Clear history” action if needed for shared devices.

## UI Flow Map

| Step | Screen | Main Content | Primary Action | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scan | Camera preview, scan frame, flashlight, history shortcut | Auto-scan | Detect QR code |
| 2 | Product found | Product name, price, stock status | Add to Cart | Add item and confirm |
| 3 | Invalid code | Error message, recovery options | Rescan | Return to scan mode |
| 4 | History | Last 5 scans with timestamps | Open item | Review or rescan past items |

## Recommended Interaction Details

- Use a **single prominent CTA** on every state to reduce hesitation.
- Show stock status with color and text, not color alone.
- Keep the product card compact so staff can scan repeatedly without extra taps.
- Add a brief success toast after adding to cart: “Added to cart.”
- If stock is low or out, keep the button visible but change copy if needed:
  - Low stock: “Add to Cart”
  - Out of stock: “Notify Manager” or disabled add action, depending on workflow

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Retail UI Patterns] https://www.nngroup.com/articles/mobile-app-navigation/

- Figma community search for scanner UI references: https://www.figma.com/community/search?query=qr%20scanner%20app%20ui

## Fast QR Scanner for Food Delivery
A minimal scanner screen should keep the camera dominant, reduce visual clutter, and surface only the actions needed to move from scan to order quickly.

## Screen Layout and Interaction Flow
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg

### 1) Live Camera Preview
- Full-screen camera feed with a subtle scan frame centered on the screen.
- Thin animated scan line to signal active scanning.
- Small hint text: “Align QR code inside the frame.”

### 2) Primary Controls
- **Flashlight toggle**: top-right, one-tap on/off.
- **Manual code entry**: compact button below the frame for typing a code if the QR is unavailable.
- Keep both controls visually light and secondary to the camera.

### 3) Recent Scans
- A compact list anchored near the lower portion of the screen.
- Each row shows restaurant name, scan time, and a quick re-open action.
- Limit to the last 3–5 scans to preserve the fast feel.

### 4) Success Bottom Sheet
- After a valid scan, slide up a bottom sheet with:
  - Restaurant name
  - Short confirmation text: “Ready to order from this place?”
  - Primary action: **Continue**
  - Secondary action: **Rescan**
- Keep the sheet partially expanded by default so the camera context stays visible.

## Minimal UI Structure
- Top bar: back, title, flashlight
- Center: live camera preview with scan frame
- Lower area: manual entry button + recent scans
- Success state: bottom sheet confirmation

## Quick Actions

## Clinic Check-In QR Scanner Interface
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg

A kiosk flow for fast self check-in at a healthcare clinic, optimized for clarity, accessibility, and minimal staff assistance. The interface uses large type, high contrast, and a simple 3-step path: scan, review, confirm.

## Recommended Screen Flow
| Screen | Purpose | Key UI Elements | Accessibility Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Welcome / Scan | Start the check-in | QR scanner viewport; “Scan patient QR code” prompt; help button | 24px+ labels; 48px+ tap targets; high-contrast border around scan area |
| 2. Appointment Review | Show matched visit details | Appointment time; doctor name; check-in status; patient name initials/avatar | Use plain language; keep critical info in 18–24px text |
| 3. Confirmation | Confirm successful check-in | Success message; estimated wait note; return-to-home timer | Large success state; no color-only meaning; audible confirmation optional |
| 4. Unreadable Code Fallback | Recover from scan failure | Manual code entry; staff assistance button; retry scan | Clear error text; avoid jargon; keep actions visible without scrolling |

## Kiosk Interaction Details
- **Welcome / Scan**
  - Full-screen camera preview with a centered scan frame.
  - Primary instruction: **“Hold QR code inside the frame”**.
  - Secondary help text: “If scanning fails, use manual entry or ask for assistance.”
  - Bottom actions:
    - **Retry Scan**
    - **Enter Code Manually**
    - **Need Help?**

- **Appointment Review**
  - Display the matched appointment in a large card:
    - **Appointment Time:** 10:30 AM
    - **Doctor:** Dr. Maya Patel
    - **Status:** Ready to check in
  - Show one primary action: **Confirm Check-In**
  - Optional secondary action: **Scan Another Code**

- **Confirmation**
  - Show a clear success state:
    - **You’re checked in**
    - “Please take a seat. We’ll call you shortly.”
  - Include a short wait-time note if available.
  - Auto-return to welcome screen after 20–30 seconds.

- **Unreadable Code Fallback**
  - Message: **“We couldn’t read that code.”**
  - Offer three recovery paths:
    - **Try Again**
    - **Enter Appointment ID**
    - **Get Staff Help**
  - Keep the error state calm and non-alarming.

## Accessibility and Visual Design
- Use a minimum body text size of **18px** and headings at **24–32px**.
- Keep buttons at least **48x48 px** with strong spacing.
- Use **high contrast** text and controls; do not rely on color alone to indicate status.
- Support screen-reader labels for:
  - scan frame
  - camera permission prompt
  - status message
  - confirmation button
- Provide a visible focus ring for keyboard navigation.
- Use simple language and avoid medical abbreviations where possible.
- Add subtle sound or vibration feedback only as a supplement, not the only confirmation.

## Quick Actions

# Boarding Pass QR Scanner UI for Travel

A clean scanner flow for boarding passes with instant trip details, a time-sensitive warning, a compact scan history, and a clear offline empty state.

## Scanner Screen Layout

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg

- Top bar: app title, help icon, and a small offline badge when disconnected.
- Main area: live camera preview with a centered scan frame and subtle corner guides.
- Primary scan hint: “Align boarding pass QR inside the frame.”
- Secondary action row: flashlight, gallery import, and manual entry.
- Result card appears immediately after a successful scan.

## Scan Result Card and Boarding Warning

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg

- **Flight number:** AA 482
- **Gate:** B14
- **Boarding time:** 06:25 PM
- **Seat:** 18C
- **Status:** Boarding soon

Warning rule:
- Show a prominent amber warning when boarding time is within **30 minutes**.
- Copy suggestion: **“Boarding starts in 18 minutes. Head to Gate B14 now.”**
- If boarding time is more than 30 minutes away, show a neutral status chip instead of the warning.

## Compact History Tab and Empty State

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock-history.svg

- History tab shows the last scanned passes in a compact list.
- Each row includes flight number, date, gate, and scan timestamp.
- Tap a row to reopen the saved boarding details.
- Keep the list short and scannable, with the newest scan at the top.

Offline-friendly empty state:
- Title: **No boarding passes scanned yet**
- Body: “Scan a QR code to load your flight details. Recent scans will stay available offline.”
- Actions:
  - **Scan Boarding Pass**
  - **Enter Manually**
- Helpful note: if offline, the UI should still show previously cached scans and the last known trip details.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Scan Flow Spec] https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/
Action: [Button: Offline UI Patterns] https://m3.material.io/foundations/interaction/overview

## Sources

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/
- Material Design 3: https://m3.material.io/
- QR code overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code

response_text:
# School Event QR Scanner

A fast check-in screen for staff to scan attendee QR codes, verify ticket status, and control entry in one place.

## Scanner Flow and Attendee States
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg

- **Primary purpose:** scan a QR code, validate the ticket, and display a clear entry decision.
- **Staff-only fallback:** manual search by name, email, or ticket ID for edge cases.
- **State handling:** success, duplicate scan, and invalid ticket are shown as distinct outcomes.

| State | What Staff Sees | Entry Result | Staff Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Success | Name, ticket type, check-in time, attendee photo/ID badge | **Allowed** | Tap to confirm entry |
| Duplicate Scan | Name, ticket type, prior scan time, warning badge | **Denied** | Review prior check-in |
| Invalid Ticket | No match or revoked ticket notice | **Denied** | Search manually or escalate |
| Manual Search | Search results with attendee details and status | Depends on record | Select attendee to verify |

## Screen Layout and Behavior
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/person-badge.svg

### Top Area
- Large scan frame with camera preview
- Status text under the frame: ready, scanning, matched, or error
- Staff-only **Manual Search** button beside the scanner controls

### After a Successful Scan
- **Name:** attendee full name
- **Ticket type:** General, VIP, Student, Staff, etc.
- **Entry permission:** Allowed / Not allowed
- **Extra detail:** gate time, scan count, or notes if needed

### Duplicate Scan State
- Highlight as already checked in
- Show first scan time and location if available
- Keep the deny action visible so staff can move the line quickly

### Invalid Ticket State
- Show “ticket not found,” “revoked,” or “expired” messaging
- Offer manual search and supervisor review
- Keep the UI calm and explicit to reduce confusion at the gate

## Staff Actions and Controls
- **Scan again** to retry the camera
- **Manual search** for attendee lookup by staff only
- **Override access** only for authorized supervisors
- **Mark issue** for tickets that need later review

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Open Scanner] https://example.com
Action: [Button: Staff Search] https://example.com/search
Action: [Button: Check-In Rules] https://example.com/policy

## Sources
- QR scanner UI pattern reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Barcode_Detection_API
- Accessible form and status design: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/
- Camera and device input guidance: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia

# Warehouse QR Scanner Screen

A clean, task-first scanner layout for fast inventory handling. The screen centers on the live scan area, then immediately surfaces item identity, stock status, and the three core actions.

## Screen Layout and Content

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg

### 1) Scanner Header
- Title: **Scan Inventory QR**
- Subtitle: “Point camera at item label”
- Status chip: **Camera Ready**
- Secondary text: Warehouse zone and aisle can appear as a small location hint

### 2) Live Scan Panel
- Large camera preview card with a centered scan frame
- Thin animated scan line for feedback
- Helper text: “Align QR label inside the frame”
- Small flashlight toggle and gallery/import icon if needed

### 3) Item Detail Card
Show the scanned item immediately after recognition:
- **Item ID:** INV-20481
- **Location:** Aisle B4, Shelf 03
- **Quantity on hand:** 128
- **Status:** Verified item or Missing item

### 4) Action Row
Primary buttons:
- **Receive**
- **Move**
- **Adjust**

Recommended button behavior:
- **Receive**: add stock to on-hand quantity
- **Move**: update storage location
- **Adjust**: correct count after cycle count or damage

### 5) Scan Log
A compact recent-activity list beneath the item card:
- 09:14 AM — INV-20481 — Verified — Aisle B4
- 09:11 AM — INV-11802 — Missing — Unmatched QR
- 09:08 AM — INV-33016 — Verified — Dock Zone 2

## Verified vs Missing Item States

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check-circle.svg

### Verified Item
- Green border or green status pill
- Item ID, location, and quantity shown in full
- Action buttons enabled
- Optional checkmark icon next to the item title

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg

### Missing Item
- Red or amber border with strong warning styling
- Show message: **“Item not found in inventory”**
- Keep Item ID visible if the QR decodes successfully
- Hide quantity or show **—**
- Disable Receive/Move/Adjust until the item is matched or manually created
- Add a small action like **Create Record** or **Review Scan** if your workflow allows it

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Open Scanner] https://www.example.com
Action: [Button: Review Scan Log] https://www.example.com

## Sources

- Material Design guidance for scan and action layouts: https://m3.material.io/
- Fluent design patterns for status and action states: https://fluent2.microsoft.design/

response_text:
## Secure Merchant QR Scanner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg

A polished banking-app flow for scanning merchant QR codes, reviewing payment details, and confirming securely before sending money.

## Payment Request Review Flow
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shield-lock.svg

### 1) Scan Merchant QR
- Camera view with a centered scan frame and subtle pulse animation
- Auto-detects merchant QR codes and pauses on successful read
- Shows a compact trust note: “Only pay after verifying merchant details”

### 2) Payment Details
- **Merchant name:** auto-filled from the QR payload
- **Amount entry:** editable currency field with keypad
- **Fee breakdown:** itemized before confirmation
  - Transfer amount
  - Service fee
  - Taxes, if applicable
  - **Total payable**
- Optional note field for payment reference

### 3) Confirmation Step
- Displays merchant name, masked merchant ID, amount, fees, and total
- Requires a deliberate confirmation action before submitting
- Supports biometric or PIN re-authentication
- Final CTA: **Confirm Payment**

### 4) Security Warning Banner
- Persistent banner appears when the QR is suspicious, malformed, expired, or mismatched
- Banner copy:
  - **Warning:** This QR code may be unsafe or invalid.
  - Do not proceed if merchant details look unfamiliar.
  - Verify the merchant name and amount before paying.
- Actions:
  - **Dismiss**
  - **Report Code**
  - **Scan Again**

## UI Components and States
| Screen State | Key Elements | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Idle Scanner | Camera preview, scan frame, help text | Waits for a valid QR code |
| QR Detected | Merchant name preview, validation chip | Checks format and merchant metadata |
| Payment Form | Amount input, fee summary, note field | Updates total in real time |
| Review Step | Full transaction summary, auth prompt | Requires biometric/PIN confirmation |
| Error / Risk | Warning banner, retry actions | Blocks payment until the code is re-scanned or verified |

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Scan QR] https://example.com/scan
Action: [Button: Review Payment] https://example.com/review
Action: [Button: Security Help] https://example.com/security

## Sources
- OWASP Mobile Security Guidance: https://owasp.org/www-project-mobile-top-10/
- PCI Security Standards Council: https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/
- NIST Digital Identity Guidelines: https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/

response_text:
## Library QR Scan Experience

A clean scan flow should confirm the book instantly, show loan status at a glance, and make the next action obvious. The history and empty state should feel lightweight, not like a separate feature.

## Scan Result and History Layout

### Scan Success Card
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg
- **Title:** Book title in a strong first line
- **Author:** Secondary line beneath title
- **Due date:** Clear date label with color emphasis when near overdue
- **Renewal eligibility:** Show as **Eligible** or **Not eligible**
- **Primary action:** **Place a hold** button
- Optional helper text: “Return or renew before the due date to avoid fines.”

### Scanned Books History
- Show the last 5–10 scans in a compact list.
- Each row should include:
  - Title
  - Scan date/time
  - Status chip: **Checked out**, **Available**, or **On hold**
  - Quick action: re-scan or view details
- Keep the list scrollable and sorted by most recent first.

### Empty State When No Scans Exist
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- **No scans yet**
- “Scan a book QR code to see title, author, due date, and hold options here.”
- Add a supportive hint: “Hold your camera over the QR code on the book label.”

## Recommended Screen Structure

| Section | What to show | UI behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Scanner header | Camera frame, scan prompt, flashlight toggle | Keep controls minimal and thumb-friendly |
| Scan result | Title, author, due date, renewal eligibility, hold button | Appear immediately after a successful scan |
| History list | Recent scanned books with status | Persist across sessions if possible |
| Empty state | Helpful message and scan hint | Show only when history is empty |

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Start Scan] https://www.example.com/library/scan
Action: [Button: View Holds] https://www.example.com/library/holds

## Sources

- QR scanning UX patterns: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/mobile-scanning-ux/
- Library account and holds concepts: https://www.oclc.org/en/services/bibs/holds.html

response_text:
## QR Repair Flow for Housing Maintenance

A clean tenant-facing scanner flow should move from **scan → verify asset → report issue → confirm submission**. Keep each screen short, mobile-first, and reassuring.

## Screen-by-Screen UI Structure

### 1) Scan Asset
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg
- Primary prompt: “Scan the QR code on the appliance or fixture”
- Helper text: “Point your camera at the asset label to identify it instantly.”
- Secondary action: manual asset code entry for damaged or unreadable labels

### 2) Asset Details
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Asset name:** e.g. Kitchen Sink Faucet
- **Issue category:** Plumbing, Electrical, HVAC, Appliance, Safety, Other
- **Warranty status:** Active, Expired, Unknown
- Show location and asset ID in smaller text for confidence

### 3) Repair Request Form
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/pencil-square.svg
- Issue description text area with short placeholder guidance
- Photo upload area for one or more images
- Optional urgency selector: Low, Normal, High
- Optional contact preference: in-app message, phone, email

### 4) Submission Confirmation
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check-circle-fill.svg
- Confirmation message: “Your repair request has been submitted.”
- Show request ID and expected next step
- Include a link to view request status

## Recommended Progress Stepper

1. Scan
2. Review Asset
3. Describe Issue
4. Upload Photos
5. Submit
6. Confirmed

Use a horizontal stepper at the top of every screen, with the current step highlighted and completed steps marked with check icons.

## Form Fields That Matter Most

- **Asset name:** read-only, prefilled from QR scan
- **Issue category:** dropdown or chips
- **Warranty status:** read-only badge
- **Problem description:** required multiline field
- **Photo upload:** camera + gallery upload
- **Submit button:** sticky at bottom for easy thumb reach

## Confirmation State

After submission, show:
- Request submitted successfully
- Ticket number
- Asset name
- Category
- Submitted time
- Next update ETA

A good confirmation screen should also offer:
- “Submit another request”
- “View request status”

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Open Scanner] https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg
Action: [Button: Add Photo] https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/camera.svg
Action: [Button: Confirm Submission] https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check-circle-fill.svg

## Sources

- Bootstrap Icons: https://icons.getbootstrap.com/
- QR code scanning pattern reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Barcode_Detection_API
- Mobile form usability guidance: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/mobile-form-design/

response_text:
## Conference QR Scanner Screen
A clean, dark-mode friendly scanner flow for fast badge lookups and networking follow-up. The layout keeps the camera view primary, then reveals attendee details and actions immediately after a successful scan.

## Screen Layout and Interaction
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg

### Top Bar
- Left: app logo or event name
- Center: **Scan Badge**
- Right: flashlight toggle and history shortcut

### Main Scanner Area
- Full-width camera preview with rounded corners
- Center scan frame with animated corner brackets
- Subtext: “Align the badge QR inside the frame”
- Dark overlay with high-contrast green or cyan scan line

### Scan Result Card
When a QR is recognized, replace the lower half with a compact attendee card:
- **Attendee name**
- Company
- Role
- Mutual interests as 2-4 pill chips
- Primary actions:
  - **Save Contact**
  - **Add Note**

### Duplicate Scan Warning
If the same badge is scanned again within the session:
- Show a slim warning banner above the result card
- Message: “Already scanned 3 minutes ago”
- Secondary line: “Open saved profile or add a new note”
- Keep the warning amber, not red, to avoid alarm fatigue

### Scan History
A scrollable list below the result card:
- Recent scans with name, company, and timestamp
- Small status dot for new vs repeated scans
- Tap any row to reopen attendee details
- Optional swipe action: add note or export contact

## Dark Mode Friendly UI Pattern
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg

### Visual Style
- Background: near-black charcoal
- Cards: slightly lighter surface with subtle borders
- Text: white and muted gray hierarchy
- Accent color: cyan, teal, or lime for scan success
- Buttons: filled primary for Save Contact, outlined secondary for Add Note

### Accessibility Details
- Large tap targets for one-handed use
- High contrast text on all surfaces
- Clear state colors for scanning, success, duplicate, and offline
- Haptic feedback on successful scan and duplicate detection

## Recommended Component Set
| Component | Purpose | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Camera preview | Scan badge QR codes | Auto-focus, torch toggle, live frame guide |
| Attendee card | Show identity details | Appears after valid scan |
| Interest chips | Surface conversation hooks | Multi-select or read-only tags |
| Save Contact button | Store attendee quickly | Saves to device or CRM |
| Add Note button | Capture follow-up context | Opens quick note sheet |
| History list | Review recent scans | Tap to reopen, filter by session |
| Duplicate banner | Prevent repeated logging | Shows last scan time and action shortcuts |

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Open Scanner UI] https://www.figma.com/community/search?query=qr%20scanner%20mobile%20ui
Action: [Button: View Dark UI Patterns] https://www.nngroup.com/articles/dark-mode-design/

## Sources
- Dark mode usability guidance: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/dark-mode-design/
- Mobile scanning interaction patterns: https://m3.material.io/components/qr-scanner/overview

response_text:
## Emergency Fund Growth at 12 Months

### Expected Ending Balances
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-dollar.svg

| Account | Rate & Compounding | Annual Fee | Ending Balance (12 mo) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Account A | 4.2% APY, monthly | $0 | **$12,504.00** |
| Account B | 4.0% APY, daily | $0 | **$12,480.00** |
| Account C | 4.35% APY, quarterly | $50 | **$12,472.00** |

### Best-to-Worst Ranking

1. **Account A** — highest net ending balance after 12 months.
2. **Account B** — slightly lower than A, but still very competitive.
3. **Account C** — highest stated APY, but the $50 fee pulls it below the others.

### Best Choice if You May Withdraw After 6 Months

- **Best practical pick: Account A**
- Why: it has the best 12-month net result among the fee-free options and is simple to hold as a liquid emergency fund.
- If you withdraw at 6 months, the fee in Account C becomes even less attractive because it reduces your return regardless of how long the money stays in the account.
- Account B is close, but Account A still edges it out on total value over the year.

### 6-Month Estimate

Using the same rates, approximate balances after 6 months are:

- **Account A:** about **$12,246**
- **Account B:** about **$12,239**
- **Account C:** about **$12,236 before fee**, or about **$12,186 net after the $50 fee**

### Quick Take
- For a full 12 months: **Account A wins**
- For a possible 6-month withdrawal: **Account A is still the safest overall choice**
- If Account C’s fee can be waived, it becomes much more competitive

### Sources
- APY and compounding basics: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-annual-percentage-yield-apy-en-121/
- Compound interest reference: https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/how-money-grows/compound-interest

response_text:
## Kyoto Spring Trip Plan
A calm, walkable 4-day Kyoto plan built around temples, food markets, and easy transit, with one half-day reserved for rest. Costs below are estimated for **2 adults** and keep the trip within your **$1,800 budget excluding flights**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan
### Day 1: Higashiyama Arrival Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, settle in the **Higashiyama** or **Gion** area for the easiest start.
- Afternoon: Gentle walk through **Sannenzaka, Ninenzaka, Yasaka Shrine, and Maruyama Park**.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original Alt=Afternoon: Gentle walk through **Sannenzaka, Ninenzaka, Yasaka Shrine, and Maruyama Park**, Kyoto, Japan
- Evening: Early dinner around **Gion**; keep the first day light and jet-lag friendly.
- Estimated cost: Lodging **$180**; local transit **$10**; meals **$70**; snacks/coffee **$20**; total **$280**.

### Day 2: Temple Circuit and Nishiki Market
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** early, then continue on foot through the surrounding temple lanes.
- Afternoon: Head to **Nishiki Market** for lunch and tasting stops; browse nearby **Teramachi** and **Shinkyogoku** shopping streets.
- Evening: Quiet dinner in central Kyoto, then a slow walk back or short transit ride.
- Estimated cost: Lodging **$180**; transit **$12**; temple entries **$12**; meals **$90**; total **$294**.

### Day 3: Arashiyama and Riverside Calm
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Take transit to **Arashiyama**; walk **Bamboo Grove** and **Tenryu-ji**.
- Afternoon: Slow riverside time, optional **Iwatayama Monkey Park** if you want a more active add-on.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/A_Japanese_Macaque_at_Arashiyama_Monkey_Park_Iwatayama%2C_Japan.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original Alt=Afternoon: Slow riverside time, optional **Iwatayama Monkey Park** if you want a more active add-on, Kyoto, Japan
- Evening: Return early and keep dinner simple near your hotel.
- Estimated cost: Lodging **$180**; transit **$18**; temple/entry fees **$18**; meals **$80**; total **$296**.

### Day 4: Rest Half-Day and Northern Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: **Half-day rest** at the hotel, a café, or a nearby bath/onsen-style spa if available.
- Afternoon: Light visit to **Nijō Castle** or **Kinkaku-ji** depending on energy; choose only one.
- Evening: Final dinner in a relaxed neighborhood such as **Demachiyanagi** or **Pontocho**.
- Estimated cost: Lodging **$180**; transit **$12**; entry **$10**; meals **$85**; rest/café time **$30**; total **$317**.

### Trip Cost Snapshot
- Lodging: **$720**
- Transit: **$52**
- Temple/attraction entry: **$52**
- Meals and snacks: **$325**
- Coffee, rest stop, small extras: **$50**
- Total estimated spend: **$1,199**

### Suggested Areas to Stay
- **Gion / Higashiyama**: Best for temple access, scenic walks, and a quieter evening atmosphere.
- **Kyoto Station area**: Best for transport convenience and easy day trips, slightly less atmospheric.
- **Karasuma / Downtown Kyoto**: Best balance of food, transit, and walkability.
- Best fit for your style: **Gion or Higashiyama**, since you prefer walking, calm neighborhoods, and temple-heavy days.

### Simple Packing Checklist
- Comfortable walking shoes
- Light layers for spring evenings
- Compact umbrella or rain shell
- Day bag with water bottle
- Portable phone charger
- Transit card or mobile payment setup
- Socks you can easily remove for temple visits
- Small cash reserve for markets and smaller shops
- Light scarf or cardigan for cooler mornings
- Reusable shopping bag for market snacks

## Best Kyoto Base for Your Style
### Recommended Stay Area: Gion / Higashiyama
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Quiet, scenic, and ideal for temple-to-temple walking.
Media: Alt=Quiet, scenic, and ideal for temple-to-temple walking, Kyoto, Japan
- Easy access to **Kiyomizu-dera, Yasaka Shrine, Maruyama Park, and central Kyoto**.
- Slight premium on price, but worth it for convenience and atmosphere.

### Backup Stay Area: Karasuma / Downtown Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Better value and strong transit access.
- Good if you want more restaurant variety and a more practical hotel choice.
- Slightly less charming than Higashiyama, but still very convenient.

response_text:
## Likely Causes for a 5-Day Dry Cough and Sore Throat
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

Based on your age, mild symptoms, no fever, and otherwise good health, this most often fits a **self-limited viral upper respiratory infection**. Penicillin allergy and no regular medications do not change the likely cause, but they matter if treatment is ever needed.

## Self-Care Checklist and Ranked Possibilities
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

### Non-emergency self-care checklist
- **Rest and fluids:** aim for steady hydration; warm drinks can soothe throat irritation.
- **Honey for cough:** 1–2 teaspoons as needed, especially before bed. Do not give honey to children under 1 year.
- **Saltwater gargles:** 1/2 teaspoon salt in a cup of warm water, gargle several times daily.
- **Throat lozenges or hard candy:** can reduce throat dryness and coughing.
- **Humidified air:** use a cool-mist humidifier or steam from a shower if the air is dry.
- **Avoid irritants:** smoke, vaping, strong fragrances, and very cold/dry air can worsen a dry cough.
- **Over-the-counter pain relief if needed:** acetaminophen or ibuprofen may help throat discomfort if you normally can take them safely.
- **Sleep support:** elevate your head slightly if coughing is worse at night.
- **Test if relevant:** if you have had any exposure or community spread, consider a home COVID test; early infections can cause this pattern.

### Possible causes, most likely to less likely
1. **Viral upper respiratory infection / common cold**
   - Most common with mild sore throat, dry cough, and low energy.
2. **COVID-19**
   - Can present without fever and with fatigue, sore throat, and dry cough.
3. **Post-nasal drip from a mild viral illness or allergies**
   - Throat irritation and cough are common, especially if you feel mucus in the back of the throat.
4. **Irritant-related throat inflammation**
   - Smoke, vaping, dry air, dust, or strong odors can trigger a dry cough.
5. **Acid reflux / laryngopharyngeal reflux**
   - Can cause throat soreness, throat clearing, and dry cough, sometimes without heartburn.
6. **Atypical bronchitis or other lower-airway irritation**
   - Less likely without fever, shortness of breath, or worsening chest symptoms.
7. **Strep throat**
   - Less likely because cough usually points away from strep, and fever is absent.

### Warning signs to seek medical care
- **Trouble breathing**, wheezing, or shortness of breath
- **Chest pain** or pressure
- **Fever that develops** or symptoms that rapidly worsen
- **Coughing up blood**
- **Severe sore throat** with trouble swallowing saliva, drooling, or muffled voice
- **Dehydration**: very dark urine, dizziness, inability to keep fluids down
- **Confusion, fainting, or marked weakness**
- **Symptoms lasting more than 10–14 days**, or a cough that is steadily worsening
- **New rash**, swollen neck glands with severe throat pain, or white patches in the throat
- **High-risk exposure** to COVID/flu with worsening symptoms, or a positive test and significant decline

## When to Check In With a Clinician
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg

- If you are **not improving after about a week**
- If the cough becomes **productive**, painful, or frequent enough to disrupt sleep despite self-care
- If you need help choosing an **OTC medicine** that fits your health history
- If you develop symptoms suggesting **strep, COVID, flu, or asthma-like wheezing**

## Sources
- CDC common cold guidance: https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/
- CDC COVID-19 symptoms: https://www.cdc.gov/covid/signs-symptoms/index.html
- NHS cough self-care and when to get help: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cough/

response_text:
## Toronto 1-Bedroom Move Plan for 2026-09-15
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

You have a **tight but workable** move window: lease end on **2026-08-31** and move-in target on **2026-09-15**. With a **CAD 2,400/month** cap including **heat + water**, hybrid work downtown, and must-haves of **pet-friendly** plus **in-unit laundry**, the search should focus on transit-friendly buildings that reduce commute friction.

## Priority Comparison for Your Apartment Search
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg

| Priority | Must / Nice-to-have | Why it matters | Search filter to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Budget | **Must** | Keeps total housing cost within your cap | Rent ≤ **CAD 2,400**, heat + water included |
| Move-in date | **Must** | You need a seamless transition after lease end | Available **2026-09-01 to 2026-09-15** |
| Downtown commute | **Must** | Hybrid schedule means commute quality still matters | Near **subway, GO, or streetcar** to downtown |
| Pet-friendly | **Must** | Avoid wasting time on no-pet buildings | Pets allowed; ask for breed/weight rules |
| In-unit laundry | **Must** | Daily convenience and a strong quality-of-life filter | Washer/dryer in suite |
| Parking | Nice-to-have | Only if you drive sometimes | Optional, compare extra cost |
| Balcony / gym / concierge | Nice-to-have | Good extras, but not worth stretching budget | Consider only if core needs are met |

## Housing Search Checklist
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check2-square.svg

### 1) Set your search frame
- Target rent: **up to CAD 2,400 all-in for heat + water**
- Preferred move-in: **2026-09-15**
- Search radius: prioritize **downtown Toronto** and transit-connected neighborhoods
- Unit type: **1-bedroom**
- Non-negotiables: **pet-friendly**, **in-unit laundry**

### 2) Build your shortlist
- Filter listings for **heat + water included**
- Confirm **in-unit laundry** is inside the suite, not shared
- Check whether the building allows **cats, dogs, or both**
- Prioritize buildings with **easy downtown commute** for your 3 office days
- Compare total monthly cost, not just base rent

### 3) Verify the unit before applying
- Ask for the **exact move-in date**
- Confirm what utilities are included
- Check if there are **pet deposits, monthly pet fees, or size limits**
- Ask about **lease term**, renewal rules, and rent increases
- Request a video tour or in-person viewing if possible

### 4) Prepare application materials
- Government ID
- Proof of income or employment
- Recent pay stubs or offer letter
- Credit report
- References from prior landlords
- Pet information if required

### 5) Protect yourself before signing
- Read the lease for **maintenance, repairs, subletting, and termination** terms
- Confirm the apartment is **vacant and ready** by your move date
- Document unit condition with photos at move-in
- Keep written proof of all promises made by the landlord or agent

## Questions to Ask Landlords
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/chat-left-text.svg

- Is **heat and water included** in the rent?
- Is the unit **actually available by 2026-09-15**?
- Is the building **pet-friendly**, and are there any breed, size, or number limits?
- Is the **laundry in-unit**, and is it exclusive to the apartment?
- What is the **total monthly cost** including any required fees?
- Are there **extra charges** for pets, parking, storage, or amenities?
- What is the **lease length** and renewal process?
- How much notice is required to end the lease?
- Is the unit **rent-controlled** or subject to any unusual annual increases?
- How long is the typical **commute to downtown Toronto** by transit from this address?
- What repairs or maintenance are the landlord’s responsibility?
- Can I see the **exact unit** or a video walkthrough before applying?
- What documents are required for the application?
- When is the **earliest move-in date** and how flexible is it?

## Best Search Strategy for Your Situation
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg

- Start with listings that match all four core filters: **budget, pet-friendly, in-unit laundry, heat/water included**
- Use commute as the next filter, because hybrid work makes location more important than extra amenities
- Be ready to trade off either building amenities or unit size before giving up the laundry or commute requirements
- If the market is tight, consider slightly expanding to areas with strong transit access rather than increasing budget first

## Sources
- Toronto Residential Tenancies: https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights
- Tenant rights and forms: https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/
- Toronto transit planning: https://www.ttc.ca/plan-a-trip

# Remote Junior Data Analyst Positioning

You have a solid base for junior analyst roles: **2 years of experience**, **strong Excel**, and **basic SQL**. To fit remote Canada roles at **CAD 65,000+**, your resume should sound more measurable, analytical, and business-focused.

# Stronger Resume Bullets and 30-Day Skill Plan

## Resume Bullet Upgrades
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/file-earmark-text.svg

- Built recurring management reports in Excel, improving visibility into key business metrics and reducing manual reporting effort.
- Developed and maintained reporting dashboards and data summaries for leadership to support faster decision-making.
- Collected, cleaned, and validated operational data to improve reporting accuracy and consistency across teams.
- Transformed raw data into clear Excel-based insights, highlighting trends, variances, and performance gaps for management review.
- Automated routine reporting tasks using advanced Excel formulas, pivot tables, and lookup functions to save time and reduce errors.
- Queried and organized data using basic SQL to support ad hoc analysis and recurring business reporting.
- Partnered with stakeholders to define reporting requirements and deliver timely, actionable data outputs.
- Supported day-to-day data operations by preparing reports, checking data quality, and resolving reporting issues quickly.

## Short Summary Statement
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/person-badge.svg

Data analyst with 2 years of experience delivering management reports, cleaning and validating data, and turning Excel and SQL outputs into actionable insights. Strong in Excel, comfortable with basic SQL, and focused on building the Python and analytics skills needed for remote Canada-based analyst roles.

## 30-Day Skill-Building Plan
### Week 1: Strengthen Excel for analysis
- Review pivot tables, XLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, SUMIFS, IFERROR, and data validation.
- Build one dashboard using charts, slicers, and conditional formatting.
- Practice cleaning messy datasets in Excel.

### Week 2: Improve SQL fundamentals
- Focus on SELECT, WHERE, JOINs, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, and subqueries.
- Write 10–15 queries against sample business datasets.
- Practice turning questions into queries.

### Week 3: Learn Python basics for analysts
- Cover variables, lists, dictionaries, pandas, and reading CSV files.
- Do simple data cleaning and summary tasks in pandas.
- Complete one mini project using a public dataset.

### Week 4: Job-ready portfolio and resume alignment
- Create 1–2 portfolio projects with clear business insights.
- Tailor your resume to remote Canadian analyst postings.
- Add keywords like reporting, dashboarding, data validation, stakeholder support, and KPI analysis.

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Build Resume Summary](https://www.linkedin.com/)
Action: [Button: Practice SQL Basics](https://www.w3schools.com/sql/)
Action: [Button: Learn Pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/)

## Sources
- Excel functions reference: https://support.microsoft.com/excel
- SQL learning reference: https://www.w3schools.com/sql/
- Pandas documentation: https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/
