response_text:
## 3-Night Madrid Dinner Plan for 4
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

Built for a **€140 total food budget**, with **1 vegetarian** and **1 gluten-free** diner, and every meal kept **under 30 minutes**. I’m assuming you’ll cook at home in Madrid using standard supermarket prices and basic pantry staples like oil, salt, pepper, and dried spices.

## 3-Day Dinner Menu and Cost Estimate
| Day | Dinner | Time | Cost for 4 | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | Chickpea, spinach, and tomato skillet with rice | 25 min | €18–€22 | Vegetarian, naturally gluten-free |
| 2 | Lemon-garlic chicken, roasted potatoes, and green beans | 30 min | €24–€30 | Easy sheet-pan style meal |
| 3 | Tuna and vegetable corn-tortilla tacos with avocado salad | 20 min | €20–€26 | Use corn tortillas for gluten-free |

### Day 1: Chickpea, Spinach, and Tomato Skillet
- **Main idea:** Sauté onion and garlic, add canned tomatoes, chickpeas, spinach, paprika, and serve over rice.
- **Easy substitutions:**
  - Add feta on top for extra richness.
  - Swap rice for quinoa if you want more protein.
  - Use smoked paprika for a more Spanish flavor.
- **Rough cost:** **€18–€22**
- **Why it works:** Cheap, filling, and fully safe for both vegetarian and gluten-free needs.

### Day 2: Lemon-Garlic Chicken with Potatoes and Green Beans
- **Main idea:** Pan-sear or roast chicken thighs with lemon, garlic, olive oil, and herbs; boil or pan-roast potatoes; steam or sauté green beans.
- **Easy substitutions:**
  - Replace chicken with halloumi or extra chickpeas for the vegetarian diner.
  - Use sweet potatoes if regular potatoes are expensive.
  - Add a side salad if you want more volume.
- **Rough cost:** **€24–€30**
- **Why it works:** Very fast, low-effort, and the same base sides can serve everyone.

### Day 3: Tuna and Vegetable Corn-Tortilla Tacos
- **Main idea:** Warm canned tuna with onion, pepper, tomato, and spices; serve in corn tortillas with avocado, lettuce, and yogurt-lime sauce.
- **Easy substitutions:**
  - Replace tuna with black beans or sautéed mushrooms for the vegetarian plate.
  - Use dairy-free yogurt if needed.
  - Add grated cheese or pickled onions for extra flavor.
- **Rough cost:** **€20–€26**
- **Why it works:** Fastest dinner of the three and easy to portion for mixed diets.

## Shopping List for 3 Dinners
### Produce
- 3 onions
- 2 heads garlic
- 2 lemons
- 1 bag spinach
- 4–5 potatoes
- 500 g green beans
- 2 tomatoes or 1 tray cherry tomatoes
- 2 bell peppers
- 1 avocado
- 1 lettuce or salad mix
- 1 lime
- Optional: fresh parsley

### Protein and Dairy
- 3 cans chickpeas
- 8 chicken thighs
- 3 cans tuna
- Optional: feta or grated cheese
- Optional: plain yogurt

### Grains and Bread Alternatives
- Rice
- Corn tortillas
- Optional: quinoa

### Pantry / Seasoning
- Olive oil
- Salt
- Black pepper
- Smoked paprika
- Dried oregano or thyme
- Canned crushed tomatoes
- Optional: cumin

### Estimated grocery total
- **Budget-friendly version:** **€62–€78**
- **With extras, cheese, and higher-end produce:** **€80–€95**
- This stays comfortably within your **€140 cap**, leaving room for breakfasts, lunch items, or snacks.

## Ingredient Swaps for Dietary Needs
- **Vegetarian option:**
  - Replace chicken or tuna with **chickpeas, black beans, mushrooms, or halloumi**.
- **Gluten-free option:**
  - Use **rice, potatoes, quinoa, and corn tortillas**.
  - Avoid soy sauce unless it is labeled gluten-free.
- **Shared meal strategy:**
  - Cook one base dish, then split at the end with a protein swap for the vegetarian portion.
  - Keep sauces and toppings separate so everyone can customize.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Find gluten-free brands] https://www.google.com/search?q=Spain+gluten-free+corn+tortillas+supermarket

## Sources
- Madrid grocery price context: https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/Madrid
- General recipe and ingredient reference: https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/
- Gluten-free ingredient guidance: https://celiac.org/gluten-free-living/what-is-gluten-free/

response_text:
# Exchange-Rate Strength Snapshot

**Context used:** I’m treating each quote as **USD per 1 unit of foreign currency**. Under that convention, a **higher number means a stronger currency vs USD**.

## Ranked Strength vs USD

| Currency | Quote (USD per 1 unit) | Rank | 250 USD converts to |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| JPY | 156.40 | 1 | JPY 39,100.00 |
| AUD | 1.52 | 2 | AUD 164.47 |
| CAD | 1.36 | 3 | CAD 183.82 |
| GBP | 1.27 | 4 | GBP 196.85 |
| EUR | 1.08 | 5 | EUR 231.48 |

## What this means

- **Strongest currency:** **JPY** by this quote format.
- **Weakest currency:** **EUR** among the five listed.
- **250 USD** buys the most units of **JPY**, and the fewest units of **EUR**.

### Conversion formula
- Foreign currency amount = **250 ÷ quote**
- Example: EUR = **250 ÷ 1.08 = 231.48 EUR**

### One caution
- Exchange-rate quotes can be written in **different directions**. A quote like “EUR 1.08” may mean either **1 EUR = 1.08 USD** or the reverse in some contexts, so always confirm whether the quote is **foreign currency per USD** or **USD per foreign currency** before comparing strength.

## Quick Actions

- Action: [Button: Convert another amount](https://www.xe.com/currencyconverter/)
- Action: [Button: Check live FX rates](https://www.oanda.com/currency-converter/en/)

## Sources

- XE Currency Converter: https://www.xe.com/currencyconverter/
- OANDA Currency Converter: https://www.oanda.com/currency-converter/en/
